sections.title: AI-Enabled Intelligent Process Automation for Modern Businesses

items.q: What is the difference between IPA and RPA?
items.a: RPA focuses on automating repetitive, rule-based tasks such as data entry, form processing, or information transfers between systems. IPA expands automation by combining AI capabilities with workflow automation, allowing organizations to process documents, analyze information, support decision-making, and automate more complex business processes across multiple systems and teams.

items.q: Which business processes can be automated with IPA?
items.a: IPA can automate approvals, document processing, reporting, customer service workflows, onboarding, procurement, and many other operational processes. Any workflow that relies on repetitive actions, multiple stakeholders, or large volumes of data is usually a strong candidate for automation.

items.q: How much do intelligent process automation services cost?
items.a: The cost depends on the complexity of the workflow, integration requirements, and the level of AI functionality involved. Some projects focus on a single process, while others automate operations across multiple departments and systems.

items.q: How long does IPA implementation take?
items.a: Smaller automation initiatives can often be delivered within a few weeks. More complex implementations involving multiple systems, integrations, and AI-powered workflows may take several months depending on project scope.

items.q: How do I know if my business is ready for intelligent process automation?
items.a: If teams spend too much time on manual processes, repetitive tasks, approvals, reporting, or transferring information between systems, automation opportunities likely exist. Working with an intelligent process automation company helps uncover bottlenecks, evaluate automation readiness, and identify the processes that will deliver the greatest operational impact.

items.q: Does your process automation comply with the EU AI Act?
items.a:
Yes. As AI systems become subject to increasing regulatory oversight, compliance is a core part of how we design and deliver automation solutions — not an afterthought.
‍
The EU AI Act introduces a risk-based framework that categorizes AI systems by their potential impact on people and organizations. For businesses adopting intelligent process automation, this means understanding how AI components within your workflows are classified, documented, and monitored.
‍
Here's what working with AltheraCode means in practice:
‍
Risk classification from day one. Before any automation is built, we assess whether AI components within your workflows fall under high-risk, limited-risk, or minimal-risk categories as defined by the EU AI Act. This shapes how we architect the system, what documentation we produce, and what controls are put in place.
‍
Transparency and explainability. High-risk AI applications require that decisions made by automated systems be traceable and explainable. We build workflows with audit trails, logging, and decision documentation that satisfy both internal governance requirements and regulatory obligations.
Human oversight by design. The EU AI Act places strong emphasis on keeping humans in control of consequential decisions. Our automation architectures include human-in-the-loop checkpoints for approval workflows, exception handling, and escalation - ensuring compliance without disrupting operational efficiency.
‍
Data governance and documentation. Compliance requires clear records of training data sources, model behavior, and system limitations. We help clients maintain the technical documentation required for conformity assessments and internal audits.
‍
Ongoing monitoring. Regulatory requirements don't end at deployment. We support continuous monitoring of AI-assisted workflows to detect performance drift, bias, or behavior changes that could trigger compliance concerns over time.
‍
Whether you're in healthcare, finance, HR, or any other sector where AI-powered automation interacts with sensitive decisions or personal data, we have the expertise to implement solutions that are both operationally effective and EU AI Act compliant.
